strings.d1.s0.name: Zinciriye Medresesi
strings.d1.s0.tips: Mardin's highest madrasa. The domed terrace overlooks the Mesopotamian plain, and mornings are cool.
strings.d1.s1.name: Mardin Grand Mosque
strings.d1.s1.tips: Artuqid minaret, set within the bazaar.
strings.d1.s2.name: Mardin Coppersmiths' Bazaar
strings.d1.s2.tips: Copper, almond candy and Mardin soap. Donkeys still haul goods along the stone lanes.
strings.d1.s3.name: Cercis Murat Konağı
strings.d1.s3.tips: Syriac-Mardin cuisine in a stone mansion with a terrace view. Order the stuffed ribs (kaburga dolması) in advance.
strings.d1.s4.name: Kasımiye Medresesi
strings.d1.s4.tips: A twin-domed madrasa with a courtyard pool. The plain turns red at sunset.
strings.d1.b0.name: Seyr-i Merdin Kafe
strings.d1.b0.tips: Terrace café for coffee and Mardin çöreği (sweet pastry).
strings.d1.b1.name: Mardin Museum
strings.d1.b1.tips: Archaeology museum in the former patriarchate. An indoor alternative to the madrasa.
strings.d2.s0.name: Deyrulzafaran Monastery
strings.d2.s0.tips: A 1,500-year-old Syriac monastery. Take the guided tour to see the sun temple and the patriarchs' tombs. Join the first group in the morning.
strings.d2.s1.name: Kırklar Church
strings.d2.s1.tips: An active Syriac church in Old Mardin with a quiet courtyard.
strings.d2.s2.name: Antik Mardin Sofrası
strings.d2.s2.tips: Ikbebet, sembusek and dobo in a mansion restaurant.
strings.d2.s3.name: Mardin Şahkulubey Konağı
strings.d2.s3.tips: A stone mansion with a courtyard, plus a walk through the bazaar lanes.
strings.d2.s4.name: Mardin Castle Viewpoint
strings.d2.s4.tips: The castle is military, but the viewpoint at its foot is open. Watch the city and plain at sunset.
strings.d2.b0.name: Mardin Kebapçısı Yusuf Usta
strings.d2.b0.tips: Mardin kebab and içli köfte (stuffed bulgur meatballs).
strings.d2.b1.name: Sakıp Sabancı Mardin City Museum
strings.d3.s0.name: Dara Ancient City
strings.d3.s0.tips: 30 km from Mardin. Roman cistern, necropolis and rock tombs, known as the 'Ephesus of Mesopotamia'.
strings.d3.s1.name: Dara Village Breakfast
strings.d3.s1.tips: Mardin breakfast in a village house, with dövme cheese (crushed-olive cheese) and bulgur with eggs.
strings.d3.s2.name: Savur
strings.d3.s2.tips: A stone town nicknamed Little Mardin, with a castle, mansions and mulberry orchards.
strings.d3.s3.name: Savur Kahveci Konağı
strings.d3.s3.tips: Mırra (bitter coffee) and mulberry molasses in a mansion.
strings.d3.b0.name: Kızıltepe Grand Mosque
strings.d3.b0.tips: An Artuqid mosque. An alternative to Savur.
strings.d3.b1.name: Dara Coffee House
strings.d4.s0.name: Midyat Konukevi
strings.d4.s0.tips: The mansion from the TV series Sıla, with a terrace and fine stonework. 1 hour from Midyat.
strings.d4.s1.name: Midyat Old Bazaar
strings.d4.s1.tips: Telkâri (silver filigree) masters and Syriac wine.
strings.d4.s2.name: Mor Barsavmo Church
strings.d4.s3.name: Midyat Kasr-ı Nehroz Restaurant
strings.d4.s3.tips: Syriac cuisine in a stone mansion: perde pilavı (pilaf baked in pastry) and alluciye.
strings.d4.s4.name: Mor Gabriel Monastery
strings.d4.s4.tips: One of the world's oldest active monasteries (397). Take the guided tour to see the mosaics. 20 km from Midyat.
strings.d4.b0.name: Midyat Gelüşke Han
strings.d4.b1.name: Hasankeyf
strings.d4.b1.tips: New Hasankeyf and the castle. An alternative to Mor Gabriel (1 hour).
strings.d5.s0.name: Mor Yakup Church Nusaybin
strings.d5.s0.tips: A 4th-century church and the excavation of the School of Nisibis, on the Syrian border.
strings.d5.s1.name: Nusaybin Zeynel Abidin Mosque
strings.d5.s1.tips: A tomb and mosque next to the church.
strings.d5.s2.name: Nusaybin Çarşı Lokantası
strings.d5.s2.tips: A town restaurant serving ribs and pilaf.
strings.d5.s3.name: Gırnavaz Mound
strings.d5.s3.tips: An Assyrian mound near Nusaybin, now an excavation site.
strings.d5.b0.name: Nusaybin Kahvaltıcısı
strings.d5.b1.name: Mardin Dara Road Viewpoint
strings.d5.b1.tips: Views over the plain. An alternative to the mound.
strings.d6.s0.name: Mardin Soap Workshop
strings.d6.s0.tips: Watch terebinth (bıttım) soap being made, and shop.
strings.d6.s1.name: Mardin Protestant Church
strings.d6.s1.tips: A restored church, now a cultural centre.
strings.d6.s2.name: Mardin Abbaralar
strings.d6.s2.tips: Vaulted lanes running beneath the houses, with cool passages.
strings.d6.s3.name: Mardin Leyli Kahvaltı
strings.d6.s3.tips: Mardin breakfast with clotted cream and honey, and sembusek (savoury pastry).
strings.d6.s4.name: Mardin Şehidiye Medresesi
strings.d6.s4.tips: A madrasa with a minaret and a tea garden. Come at sunset.
strings.d6.b0.name: Mardin Mırra Evi
strings.d6.b1.name: Latifiye Mosque
strings.d6.b1.tips: An Artuqid mosque. An alternative to Şehidiye.
strings.d7.s0.name: Mardin Almond Candy Shop
strings.d7.s0.tips: Almond candy, Mardin soap and telkâri (silver filigree) souvenirs.
strings.d7.s1.name: Mardin 1st Street
strings.d7.s1.tips: Old Mardin's main street. Take a last walk.
strings.d7.s2.name: Mardin Kahvaltı Konağı
strings.d7.b0.name: Mardin Maristan Kafe
strings.d7.b0.tips: A café in a former Artuqid hospital, with mırra and a terrace.
strings.d7.b1.name: Emir Hamamı Mardin
strings.d7.b1.tips: An Artuqid-era hammam. Say goodbye with a scrub and foam massage.
strings.note0: Mardin Airport is 20 minutes from the city. A car is useless in Old Mardin, so walk. For Midyat, Dara and Nusaybin, take a car or minibus.
strings.note1: Order the stuffed ribs (kaburga dolması) in advance at Cercis Murat. Mırra is bitter coffee, and you hand the cup back. Almond candy and terebinth soap make good souvenirs.
strings.note2: In winter, days are mild (10-15°C) and nights are cold. The best season is March to April; snow is rare.
strings.note3: Respect service times at Syriac churches and monasteries. Deyrulzafaran is entered on a guided tour, and short sleeves are not allowed.
strings.note4: The streets of Old Mardin are steep and paved with stone, so wear comfortable shoes and cool off in the abbaralar.
strings.note5: Sunset at Kasımiye is Mardin's most famous sight. Arrive 1 hour early.
